column1: # Members renamed by Mojang between 1.21.11 and 26.3 (26.x keeps Mojang names, so intermediary cannot see these).
# Also applied to plain (non-SRG) names in old bytecode, such as enum constants.

column4: 26.3 PushReaction declares PUSH_PULL, PUSH, POPPED, IMMOVEABLE, IGNORE_ENTITY; 1.21.11 NORMAL meant "pushed and pulled by pistons" = PUSH_PULL
26.3 PushReaction declares PUSH_PULL, PUSH, POPPED, IMMOVEABLE, IGNORE_ENTITY; 1.21.11 DESTROY meant "broken (popped off) when pushed" = POPPED
26.3 PushReaction declares PUSH_PULL, PUSH, POPPED, IMMOVEABLE, IGNORE_ENTITY; 1.21.11 BLOCK meant "pistons cannot move it" = IMMOVEABLE
26.3 PushReaction declares PUSH_PULL, PUSH, POPPED, IMMOVEABLE, IGNORE_ENTITY; 1.21.11 IGNORE meant "entities are not moved by it" = IGNORE_ENTITY
26.3 PushReaction declares PUSH_PULL, PUSH, POPPED, IMMOVEABLE, IGNORE_ENTITY; 1.21.11 PUSH_ONLY meant "can be pushed but not pulled" = PUSH
1.20.5 renamed AttributeModifier.Operation.ADDITION to ADD_VALUE; enum constants keep plain names in Forge 1.20.1 bytecode, so only an owner rename reaches them
1.20.5 renamed AttributeModifier.Operation.MULTIPLY_BASE to ADD_MULTIPLIED_BASE; enum constants keep plain names in Forge 1.20.1 bytecode, so only an owner rename reaches them
1.20.5 renamed AttributeModifier.Operation.MULTIPLY_TOTAL to ADD_MULTIPLIED_TOTAL; enum constants keep plain names in Forge 1.20.1 bytecode, so only an owner rename reaches them
1.21.2 InteractionResult has no CONSUME_PARTIAL; it meant "consumed, without the item use animation" = CONSUME
